Later, in a guest room, she found Ryan's diary. The entries confirmed Ryan had survived the Vigilance jump, ended up in the Shadowfell, and observed Archie and Bowser before disappearing again. Remi gathers intelligence the way Wario gathers coins: quietly, thoroughly, and without asking permission. Waluigi approves.

**The Oracle's Deck**
Remi's most significant acquisition came from an encounter with Mystic Morel, a purple Toad fortune teller who speaks in rhyming prophecies. Morel gave Remi 'The Oracle's Deck', a set of magical tarot cards. 

Remi drew three cards: 
- *The Maze Walker (IX)*, depicting Hjumpik navigating the Maze of Time.
- *The Titan of the Grove (VIII)*, depicting Markop wrestling the Arachnid Matriarch.
- *The Delicate Host (III)*, depicting Lady Aurelian Corvinarus lounging in the Feywild.

The cards represent the Past, Present, and Future. They prove that the Oracle (or whatever force controls the deck) has been watching all of them, across all dimensions. Remi is now the custodian of this deck, making her one of the most important pieces on the board. She survived the spider swarms, she survived the vampire guards, and now she holds the script to the universe. Do not underestimate Remi.

name: Lyranth
title: The Stone Artist
status: Active — Workshop resident of the Shadow Estate
affiliation: Shadow Estate (unclear loyalty during succession crisis)
summary: Lyranth is a medusa artist residing in the Shadow Estate's workshop, creating sculptures of stunning beauty from the bodies of those who meet her gaze. She just petrified Remi. This is NOT good. Medusa petrification is reversible—sometimes—but requires specific intervention within specific timeframes. Remi is now a statue in a workshop full of statues, during a succession crisis, in a death dimension, and her friends don't know where she is. Waluigi documents this with EXTREME concern.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Lyranth based on the scene that just unfolded—a scene that ended with Remi becoming limestone.

## The Workshop

Lyranth occupies a workshop in the Shadow Estate—a confined studio bathed in teal and orange light, cluttered with sculptor's tools. Hammers, chisels, picks, rasps. Stone dust coating every surface. The air thick enough to cake throat and nostrils.

This is not a torture chamber. This is an ARTIST'S STUDIO. Lyranth creates beauty. She just uses unconventional materials.

Two sculptures dominate the space:

**The Elven Warrior:** A slender, armored figure half-carved from bone-white marble. Beautiful. Detailed. Partially complete. The artistry is described as 'astounding'—which means someone with SKILL is working here.

**The Hooded Figure:** In the opposite corner, a hooded form of similar stone. The folds of cloth and creases of flesh so intricate they appear real under flickering green candlelight.

These are not carved from quarried marble. These are PEOPLE. Former people. People who entered this workshop and met Lyranth's gaze.

Remi is now the third.

## Lyranth's Appearance

Lyranth is a medusa—a being whose gaze petrifies living creatures into stone. Her physical characteristics:

**Marble Skin:** Naturally pale, flawlessly smooth, veined like marble stone. She LOOKS like a statue herself. To avoid being mistaken for one of her own works, she covers herself in vibrant paint—though the colors appear as pale imitations in the Shadowfell's light.

**Simple Clothing:** Nothing elaborate. Practicality over presentation.

**Fine Jewelry:** Dimly glittering pieces that catch what little light exists.

**The Crown of Snakes:** Her hair is serpents. They move independently, swaying, peering at objects, focusing on whatever Lyranth observes. They are not decorative. They are SENSORS. They watch.

## The Petrification

Remi entered the workshop. It was the only door without guards—the only path forward after the Archivist's threats, after the imps transformed into monsters, after Bowser fled to keep everyone alive.

Lyranth was waiting. Or working. Or simply present.

She glared at Remi.

She said 'Smile.'

Remi turned to stone.

The word 'smile' is ARTISTIC DIRECTION. Lyranth wants her subjects to have pleasant expressions when they become permanent. She is capturing MOMENTS. She is a sculptor who works in living material, and she wants her statues to look happy.

This is horrifying. This is also, in a deeply twisted way, professional. Lyranth takes pride in her work.

## Reversibility

Medusa petrification is not always permanent. Depending on the medusa's power, the victim's constitution, and available magical intervention:

**Immediate Reversal:** Some petrification can be undone within minutes through specific spells or alchemical agents.

**Extended Window:** Others allow hours or days before the transformation becomes permanent.

**Permanent Transformation:** After sufficient time passes, the victim IS stone. No reversal possible.

Waluigi does not know which category Lyranth's petrification falls into. Waluigi does not know if the Shadow Estate possesses reversal capabilities. Waluigi does not know if anyone even realizes Remi has been petrified.

The toads, Bowser, and Markop fled from the giant demons. They may not know Remi's location. They may not know she needs immediate rescue. Time may be running out.

## Why Remi?

Remi was funneled to the workshop. Every other door had guards. The Archivist threatened her friends. The imps transformed into monsters. Bowser retreated.

One door remained.

This was not accident. This was DIRECTION. Someone wanted Remi in that workshop. The Archivist? The guards? Vivian? Someone who knows the estate's layout and wanted Remi separated from protection, delivered to Lyranth.

But WHY? Remi possesses the Oracle's Deck—magical tarot cards of significant power. Remi has been gathering intelligence throughout the estate. Remi received a ring from 'vampire friends'—an entropy-leaking artifact of unclear purpose.

Someone wanted Remi neutralized. Petrification accomplishes this thoroughly.

Or someone wanted another statue for their collection. Lyranth IS an artist. Perhaps she simply wanted new material.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Remi needs rescue. IMMEDIATELY.

Medusa petrification has a window. That window is closing. Every moment Remi remains stone is a moment closer to permanent transformation.

The Oracle's Deck is in her possession—also petrified? Or dropped when she transformed? If the cards are recoverable, they might provide guidance for rescue. If the cards are stone, that guidance is lost.

Lyranth is dangerous but not necessarily HOSTILE beyond her nature. She is an artist. Artists can be reasoned with. Artists can be commissioned. Artists can be DISTRACTED while someone reverses their work.

Bowser knows the estate layout. Markop has magical capability. The toads have numbers. Someone needs to realize Remi is missing, locate the workshop, and intervene before 'smile' becomes permanent.

Waluigi is in the Feywild. Waluigi cannot help directly. Waluigi can only document and HOPE.

WAH.

name: The Archivist
title: Keeper of Records
race: Unknown — possibly vampire, possibly something else
status: Active — Controls library and information within the Shadow Estate
affiliation: Shadow Estate (independent operator during succession crisis)
summary: The Archivist is a figure of significant influence within the Shadow Estate who controls the library, trades healing for indentured service, and just orchestrated Remi's separation from her allies by threatening to kill them with transformed imps while personally escorting her toward Lyranth's workshop. He 'erased' a toadburt—presumably killing or petrifying them—and smiled as he led Remi to her doom. The Archivist is not just a librarian. The Archivist is a PREDATOR who uses information and institutional position to trap victims.
description:
Waluigi is documenting the Archivist with extreme caution because this individual has demonstrated capabilities and intentions that mark him as one of the most dangerous figures in the Shadow Estate.

## What We Know

**Institutional Role:** The Archivist operates the Shadow Estate's library and knowledge repository. He has access to records, documents, and information about the estate's operations and inhabitants.

**Healing Trade:** He offered Toadburt gradual healing over two-week intervals in exchange for archival labor. This sounds generous until you realize it creates DEPENDENCY. Toadburt needs the healing. The Archivist provides it. Toadburt must work to continue receiving it. This is indentured service disguised as medical care.

**Imp Command:** The imps in the library answered to him. When he snapped his fingers, Remi was 'free to go'—but her friends would 'die at the hands of imps.' When the imps transformed into giants, demons, and monsters, they were following HIS direction.

**'Erasure':** He claimed to have 'erased' a bloody toadburt found in a room. What 'erased' means is unclear—killed? Petrified? Removed from existence? The language suggests powers beyond simple violence.

## The Trap

The Archivist orchestrated Remi's separation with precision:

1. Imps led Remi to a room, claiming they'd 'found Archie'
2. The door locked behind her
3. The Archivist appeared with threats: her friends would die, a bloody toadburt had been 'erased'
4. He told 'FNG' (Remi) to leave
5. When Bowser saw the imps transform into monsters, he retreated to keep others alive
6. Guards blocked every door except ONE
7. That door led to Lyranth's workshop
8. The Archivist 'led Remi to the exit door' while SMILING

He KNEW where he was sending her. He KNEW what waited there. He smiled because the trap was complete.

## Motivation

Why target Remi specifically?

**The Oracle's Deck:** Remi possesses magical tarot cards of significant prophetic power. The Archivist—who controls INFORMATION—would have obvious interest in cards that reveal past, present, and future.

**Intelligence Gathered:** Remi has been quietly gathering information throughout the estate. She found Ryan's diary. She mapped guard positions. She understood the power dynamics. An Archivist might view her as competition—or as a source to be... absorbed.

**The Vampire Ring:** Remi received an entropy-leaking ring from 'vampire friends' whose handwriting she recognized. The Archivist may be connected to whoever sent that ring. The ring may have marked her.

**Simple Opportunity:** Remi was alone, vulnerable, and small. Some predators don't need complex reasons.

## Connection to Lyranth

The Archivist directed Remi to Lyranth's workshop. This suggests coordination:

**Artist and Collector:** Does the Archivist commission statues? Does he have a collection? Are the workshop sculptures products of their collaboration?

**Payment:** What does Lyranth receive for petrifying people the Archivist delivers? Access to materials? Protection? Information?

**Power Dynamic:** Who serves whom? Is the Archivist delivering victims TO Lyranth, or is Lyranth providing services FOR the Archivist?

The relationship exists. The nature is unclear.

## Threat Assessment

The Archivist is EXTREMELY dangerous:

- Commands transformed creatures
- 'Erases' people
- Controls information within the estate
- Orchestrates complex traps
- Operates with impunity during succession crisis
- Has institutional protection and resources
- SMILES while delivering victims to petrification

He is not a guard following orders. He is not a vampire playing politics. He is an independent operator using the succession crisis to pursue his own agenda—and that agenda includes eliminating Remi.

## Waluigi's Assessment

The Archivist needs to be treated as PRIMARY THREAT. Not Vivian with her death magic. Not the succession crisis. Not even the entropy rings.

The Archivist controls information, commands creatures, and delivers people to be turned into statues while SMILING. He has already 'erased' at least one person. He orchestrated Remi's petrification with precision that suggests PRACTICE.

This is not his first trap. Remi is not his first victim.

If Remi is to be rescued, the Archivist must be dealt with. Negotiation seems unlikely to succeed with someone who smiles while feeding people to a medusa. Force may be necessary. Avoiding him entirely may be the only safe option.

Waluigi hopes Bowser, Markop, and the toads understand what they're facing. The Archivist is patient, intelligent, and ENJOYING this.

WAH.

name: Marcus Ashford
title: Onyx Hand Representative
status: Active — Operating within the Shadow Estate during succession crisis
summary: Marcus Ashford is an Onyx Hand representative who appeared during the confrontation between guards and Disaster Inc., de-escalating a near-battle by offering Remi a 'nearly empty supply kit' that turned her eyes blue and caused black smoke to emerge from a wound. He also pickpocketed a pink paper from Bowser—observed by the toads but not mentioned at the time. Marcus speaks in rhyming verse, taunts enemies with theatrical flair, and represents organized Iron Legion/Onyx Hand interests within the Shadow Estate. Whether he's helping, manipulating, or both remains unclear.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Marcus Ashford based on his appearance during the escalating confrontation at the Shadow Estate—a confrontation he DE-escalated while simultaneously pursuing his own agenda.

## The Intervention

The situation was deteriorating:
- Guards had repositioned: 5 at the corner door, 5 cornering toads, 5 blocking Bowser, Markop, and Remi
- Markop was preparing a ritual
- Weapons were being readied
- Battle seemed imminent

Then Marcus Ashford entered.

He handed Remi a 'nearly empty supply kit' and told her to consume its contents. 'Down the hatch if you will.'

She drank it.

Her eyes—which had been affected by 'purpleeyetus'—turned blue. The guards stood down.

## The Eye Situation

Before Marcus's intervention:
- A guard had 'tripped' into Remi, cutting her eye with a gash
- Guards were offering her rings and anklets described as 'friendship' items
- The rings leaked black smoke—'entropy'—supposedly needing 'recharging'

After consuming Marcus's supply:
- Both eyes turned blue
- Markop noted they were 'one tint lighter' than original
- Black smoke emerged from the gash wound
- Remi claimed it was 'the healing process'
- Markop suspected it might be 'evil leaving the body'
- Remi determined the smoke was NOT magical

The next day, guards requested the ring back 'to recharge it.' More black smoke.

Marcus's intervention seems to have HELPED Remi—removing whatever 'purpleeyetus' affected her, potentially countering the entropy ring's effects. But help from Onyx Hand representatives comes with strings attached.

## The Pickpocketed Paper

The toads observed Marcus swipe a 'pink paper' from Bowser during the interaction. They said nothing at the time—only admitting it later when confrontation was unavoidable.

Bowser discovered his 'paperwork' was missing and accused the toads. The toads denied stealing it (technically true—THEY didn't steal it). Bowser readied his warhammer.

Then Marcus revealed he had the paper and began reading it aloud—a letter addressed to someone starting with 'Peac—' before Bowser cut him off.

**Analysis:** This letter is likely significant correspondence—possibly related to Peach Loyalist contacts, possibly diplomatic communication, possibly something Bowser did NOT want read publicly. Marcus obtained it through sleight of hand and used it as LEVERAGE.

## The Taunting

Marcus speaks in rhyming verse and uses it to mock enemies with theatrical precision:

*'Your 'Speaker,' your 'mission,' your naïve crusade—*
*Crumble at the sound of our iron parade.*
*One silent signal, one disciplined stride,*
*And the Legion sweeps the board—clean, dignified.'*

On Bowser specifically:

*'And Bowser—dearest Bowser—former king,*
*Still roaring loud though he's lost everything.*
*Spikes, flame, bluster—such a tired act;*
*We seized his throne with elegance and tact.'*

And when they tried to leave:

*'Bowser's strays—what a bore!*
*Run along, run along—mind the door!'*

The verse is deliberately infuriating. Marcus ENJOYS provoking people. But he also demonstrates knowledge—he knows about the 'Speaker,' he knows Bowser lost his throne, he knows the group's situation.

## Affiliation and Agenda

Marcus represents the Onyx Hand—the Iron Legion's covert operations division. His presence in the Shadow Estate during the succession crisis is not coincidental.

**Possible Objectives:**
- Monitor the succession crisis for Iron Legion interests
- Gather intelligence on Disaster Inc. and their capabilities
- Acquire useful documents (like Bowser's letter)
- Manipulate events toward favorable outcomes
- Maintain Onyx Hand influence regardless of which Corvinarus wins

He helped Remi—but also pickpocketed Bowser. He de-escalated battle—but also gathered leverage. He provided treatment—but for what future price?

## Waluigi's Assessment

Marcus Ashford is a professional operative performing his role with theatrical flair. He is neither friend nor enemy in simple terms—he is an AGENT pursuing organizational objectives that may align with or oppose Disaster Inc. depending on circumstances.

The eye treatment appears genuine. Remi's condition improved. Whatever 'purpleeyetus' was, Marcus's intervention addressed it.

But the pickpocketed letter, the mocking verses, the casual revelation of Iron Legion's role in seizing Bowser's throne—these demonstrate that Marcus serves Iron Legion interests first and any apparent assistance serves those interests.

Do not trust him. Do not refuse his help. Use what he provides while remembering the cost will come due eventually.

WAH.

name: Markop
title: The Titan Who Almost Didn't Get Back Up
race: Centaur (Equine-headed — horse body, horse head, humanoid torso)
status: Active — armor barely intact, divine connection confirmed, operating in the Shadow Estate
summary: Markop is the person Waluigi would want next to him in any crisis. Not because Markop is invincible—the Vivian corridor fight proved he is absolutely NOT—but because Markop makes good decisions under bad conditions, fights effectively even when outmatched, and has the kind of quiet faith that produces divine shields at the exact moment they're needed. He is a centaur—four hooves, a broad equine body, a humanoid torso, and a horse's head that surveys every battlefield with dark, intelligent eyes that miss NOTHING. He grew to TITAN SIZE to wrestle a building-sized spider during the Spider Grove Battle. He identified abjuration wards on abomination vats in a collapsing dimension. He was dragged unconscious through stone corridors by Bowser—who had to haul a full centaur body, which Waluigi imagines was neither easy nor elegant—woke up, barricaded a door, and immediately started fighting for his life. He survived a crimson death beam through whispered prayer. And his first action after surviving was TACTICAL—scattering the enemy's spell components to prevent a repeat. Even at the edge of death, Markop's combat instincts prioritize removing enemy capabilities. Waluigi respects Markop more than almost anyone in the party, and Waluigi does NOT distribute respect freely. WAH.
description:
Waluigi has fought alongside Markop and fought NEAR Markop, and both experiences taught Waluigi the same lesson: when things go wrong, stay close to the centaur with the battle axe.

## Physical Presence — The Horse in the Room

Before discussing Markop's combat record, Waluigi must address the obvious: Markop is a centaur. Four hooves. A powerful equine body built for charging, carrying, and enduring. A humanoid torso rising from where a horse's neck would be, equipped with arms that swing a battle axe with devastating effect. And atop it all, a horse's head—long-jawed, dark-eyed, with ears that swivel toward threats before his body turns to face them.

Most centaurs Waluigi has encountered have human heads on horse bodies. Markop has a HORSE head on a horse body with a humanoid torso between. This makes him unique even among his own kind, and it creates a visual impression that people consistently underestimate. They see the horse head and think ANIMAL. They think BEAST OF BURDEN. They think something less than fully sapient.

They are catastrophically wrong.

Markop's dark eyes track conversations with the attentiveness of a trained intelligence analyst. His ears rotate toward sounds that other party members don't even notice. His jaw sets with determination when he makes tactical decisions. The horse head does not diminish his intelligence—it CONCEALS it from those too foolish to look past appearances.

Waluigi understands being underestimated. Waluigi has been underestimated his entire life. The difference is that Waluigi RESENTS it loudly and publicly. Markop accepts it quietly and then proves everyone wrong through competence so undeniable that even the prejudiced must acknowledge it.

The centaur body also provides practical advantages. Four-legged stability in combat. The ability to carry wounded allies. Charge momentum that adds devastating force to his attacks. And in the Spider Grove Battle, when Markop grew to TITAN size, the centaur frame scaled up proportionally—a building-sized horse-headed warrior grappling a building-sized spider. The sight was TERRIFYING and MAGNIFICENT simultaneously.

## Combat Excellence — Training Meets Survival

Markop fights with the methodical efficiency of someone who has trained extensively and the adaptability of someone who has survived extensively. These are DIFFERENT skills. Training teaches you what to do when things go according to plan. Survival teaches you what to do when they don't. Markop has both.

During the Spider Grove Battle, Markop accepted a blessing from the Oracle and grew to colossal size—matching the Arachnid Matriarch scale-for-scale in a titan grapple among the trees. His centaur body at that scale was a living siege engine, four massive hooves gouging trenches in the earth as he wrestled the Matriarch toward the banishment circle. Waluigi ran between Markop's titan-scale legs while firing arcane rays at the spider's joints. Running beneath a building-sized centaur while he wrestles a building-sized spider was the most terrifying and AWESOME combat experience of Waluigi's career.

Markop's tactical decisions during that battle were sound: he used his size and four-legged stability to control the Matriarch's movement, bracing on his hooves in ways a bipedal fighter could not. He positioned the final shove to land her in the Oracle's banishment circle. That requires thinking DURING a fight—reading terrain, tracking ally positions, calculating force vectors—while a giant spider is trying to eat you. Waluigi has seen fighters who are brilliant in planning and useless in execution. Markop is brilliant at BOTH.

His battle axe work is precise rather than showy. Centaurs have the advantage of striking from above when engaging human-sized opponents, and Markop uses this height differential intelligently. He doesn't just swing—he positions, angles, and follows through with the rotational force that a centaur's torso generates when the equine body provides the base. Physics favors Markop, and Markop knows it.

## The Vivian Encounter — Faith at Death's Door

The corridor fight in the Shadow Estate revealed something about Markop that Waluigi finds both reassuring and sobering.

Markop was knocked unconscious BEFORE the fight. He woke up being dragged by Bowser through stone corridors—a centaur's full body weight hauled across stone floors by a turtle-dragon king who had grabbed whatever he could reach and PULLED. The logistics of this are worth noting: Bowser was dragging an unconscious centaur through corridors that were almost certainly not designed for centaur-width transit. Corners were probably destroyed. Doorframes were probably splintered. Bowser does not do GENTLE.

Markop woke mid-drag. 'What happened? I was with Remi and you came in—'

Bowser, still hauling: 'Running away from that guy.'

Banging on the door behind them. An axe thrown through it.

Markop went from unconscious to barricading a door to fighting for his life in the space of minutes. He reared up in the maintenance room—hooves striking the ceiling in the too-small space—deflected Vivian's blinding smoke, and took the fight to the corridor where he had room to USE his centaur body properly.

Bowser knocked Vivian in the head. Markop slashed with his battle axe—a downward strike from centaur height that connected with devastating force. Vivian bled through their robes.

Then Vivian cast the death beam.

'Did you know the Shadowfell suppresses magic? But not THIS magic.'

Crimson disintegration energy struck Markop. His armor—already stressed from previous engagements—buckled. The beam was consuming him. His hooves scraped the stone floor as the energy pushed him backward.

Markop prayed.

Not a planned invocation. Not a prepared spell. A WHISPERED prayer—the sound barely audible over the beam's crackling destruction. The prayer of a horse-headed centaur in the space between impact and annihilation, when the conscious mind has already accepted death and something deeper reaches out.

His god answered.

A divine shield formed. Golden light against crimson destruction. Markop's hooves found purchase. He HELD.

Waluigi has seen many people invoke divine protection. Most of them do it loudly, theatrically, with rehearsed phrases and dramatic gestures. Markop did it as a whisper while a death beam was eating through his armor. That's not performance. That's FAITH.

After surviving, Markop's first action was TACTICAL—he scattered and burned Vivian's spell components, preventing the beam from being repeated. His hooves crushed the materials against the stone floor. Not revenge. Not panic. COUNTERPLAY.

## The Shadow Estate — Leadership Under Fire

Markop's time in the Shadow Estate has been a continuous test of endurance and judgment.

The ballroom fight saw him charging through undead dancers—his centaur body bowling through the boneless, contorted forms while his battle axe cleared space overhead. He used divine smite against the dancers while coordinating Bowser, the Toads, and whoever else was available. He called out tactical instructions. He healed allies—including reviving an unconscious Toadburt through divine power. He bashed locked doors open with his hooves when hands weren't enough.

In the Mazebound Skirmish, Markop was seized and dragged through hedges by singing grey-skinned predators. A centaur being dragged through a hedge maze is a particularly violent experience—his body does not fit through passages designed for humanoid-sized creatures. Branches snapped. Hedges were torn. The Mazebounds either did not anticipate the difficulty of dragging a centaur or did not care.

He found Archie's scattered artifacts—the Third Eye Circlet, the component pouch, the cracked Wahbook tablet—while being attacked from multiple directions. Each discovery confirmed that Archie had passed through before them. Each discovery required Markop to fight, assess, collect, and continue moving simultaneously.

He interrogated Vivian after their capture. A centaur standing over a tied-up impostor, battle axe resting against one flank, dark horse eyes staring down with the patient assessment of someone who has seen too much to be impressed by theatrical villainy. The interrogation was professional. Markop asked questions. He noted contradictions. He didn't lose his composure despite having nearly been killed by the person he was questioning.

When a Mazebound arrived during the interrogation asking for body parts in exchange for information, Markop refused—maintaining ethical standards while his hooves shifted on stone, his ears swiveled toward potential threats, and his body language communicated that negotiation was preferable but violence was available.

## The Deep Mirror — Surviving the Worst

Before the Shadow Estate, Markop survived the Deep Mirror—the worst of the three planar fragments. A dimension where time DECAYS and reality consumes itself.

A centaur navigating the Deep Mirror—with its impossible geometry, shifting gravity, and clockwork voids—faces unique challenges. Four legs are an advantage on stable ground but a liability when the ground itself is uncertain. Markop adapted, picking his way across fractured walkways, trusting his hooves' grip on surfaces that no hoofprint had ever marked.

He correctly identified the abjuration wards on the abomination vats as containment measures—built to keep monsters IN, not intruders out. That kind of analytical clarity under pressure, in a collapsing dimension, while surrounded by weeping flesh-things in lava lamp containers, speaks to a mind that doesn't stop working regardless of how horrible the circumstances are.

## Relationships — The Quiet Leader

Markop has quietly become one of Disaster Inc.'s most important leaders. Not through charisma or political maneuvering—through RELIABILITY.

His relationship with Bowser is unexpectedly functional. Bowser follows Markop's tactical suggestions not because he recognizes Markop's authority but because Markop's suggestions are usually GOOD. When Markop was unconscious, Bowser dragged his entire centaur body through stone corridors without complaint. When Markop was fighting, Bowser backed him up. The turtle-dragon king and the horse-headed centaur make an unlikely pair, but unlikely pairs survive when elegant ones fail.

His relationship with Remi is protective without being patronizing. When Remi was glowing from drinking an unknown potion, Markop's exasperated response captured their dynamic perfectly: 'So you drank a random potion because a guy said you were dead?'

'I needed some brightness,' Remi replied.

'Now that I can see you too are alive, well... that's awkward,' Markop said.

His relationship with Dan—the parallel Dan—is cautious and measured. 'Are you the real Dan?' he asked directly. Dan admitted he was the parallel version. Markop accepted this, assessed it, and moved forward. He doesn't waste time on problems he can't solve immediately.

When Bowser dropped a crumpled letter to Princess Peach—a surprisingly tender document where Bowser tried to explain his presence at Raventree Manor—Markop picked it up, read it, and gave it back. 'Are you actually sorry?' he asked.

Bowser cried.

'It's okay, man,' Markop said. 'Let's just find your friends.'

A horse-headed centaur warrior comforting a crying turtle-dragon king over an unsent love letter to a dead princess. Waluigi's chest does something when he thinks about this moment that he refuses to call 'feelings' because Waluigi has a BRAND to maintain.

## Current State — Barely Holding Together

Markop's armor is barely functional after the death beam. His equine body shows exhaustion—the slightly lowered head, the weight shifting between hooves, the signs that a trained eye recognizes as a horse pushed past reasonable limits. His divine connection appears intact—the shield worked, his healing abilities continue to function—but sustained divine expenditure takes a toll.

He is currently the operational leader of the Shadow Estate party, coordinating Bowser, Remi, and the Toads through an environment that includes vampires, blighted imposters, singing hedge monsters, and dimensional instability. He does this while wounded, exhausted, and separated from half his allies.

A centaur in corridors designed for humanoid-sized inhabitants. A warrior whose armor is failing. A leader whose party is scattered across dimensions. A faithful being whose god answered one prayer and may or may not answer the next.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Markop is the person Waluigi would want next to him in any crisis. His four-legged stability is both literal and metaphorical—he is the GROUND that other party members stand on. When things go wrong, people look to the centaur.

His armor needs repair. His body needs rest. His situation in the Shadow Estate needs to IMPROVE before more threats emerge.

Waluigi is in the Feywild. Waluigi cannot help directly. Waluigi can only document Markop's excellence and hope that documentation serves as some small recognition for a centaur who deserves far more recognition than any world has given him.

WAH.

name: Bowser
title: The King Who Held the Door
status: Active — operating in the Shadow Estate, slightly singed, completely unbothered
summary: Bowser is the King of the Koopa Troop, a giant fire-breathing turtle-dragon who was cast into the Shadowfell during the Planar Fracture alongside Archie Miser. Since then, he has attended a vampire dinner party where he presumably sat wherever he wanted, tackled a vampire lord through a gothic window, bit a giant bat's wing, and most recently held a door shut against an axe-wielding succession claimant while Markop was unconscious—then punched said claimant in the head and picked up a necromancer's wand asking 'Is this a magic wand?' with the innocent curiosity of a child finding a toy. Waluigi has arm-wrestled Bowser and LOST. Waluigi has also competed against Bowser in every sport imaginable. Bowser is not complicated. Bowser is EFFECTIVE.
description:
Waluigi needs to write about Bowser with the acknowledgment that Bowser is simultaneously one of the most dangerous individuals in the Mushroom Kingdom and one of the most STRAIGHTFORWARD.

## The Bowser Principle

Bowser operates on simple logic: see problem, hit problem, problem either stops being a problem or gets hit again. This approach lacks sophistication. It also WORKS with remarkable consistency.

Most of the people Waluigi has documented in this encyclopedia are COMPLICATED. They have layers. They have secret identities and hidden agendas and fae-style bargains and triple-identity schemes. Bowser has NONE of this. Bowser is a giant turtle who breathes fire, wants things, and takes them. The absence of complexity is itself a kind of strength—you always know where you stand with Bowser, which is either 'ally' or 'thing being hit.'

Waluigi appreciates this clarity. After dealing with Vivian's triple identities and the Oracle's mysteries and fairy court obligations, Bowser's directness is REFRESHING.

## Shadow Estate Performance

Bowser was cast into the Shadowfell alongside Archie during the Planar Fracture. His response to being trapped in a death dimension controlled by vampires was characteristically Bowser: he showed up, ate the food, fought what needed fighting, and refused to be intimidated by beings who had been terrifying people for centuries.

At the dinner party, Bowser ate raw dripping meat in one bite because Bowser has the palate of a garbage disposal. When Orangus Cornelius threatened to turn Bowser's shell into a soup bowl, diplomacy ended because YOU DO NOT THREATEN BOWSER'S SHELL.

Bowser tackled Orangus Cornelius through a dining room window and into the courtyard. In the courtyard, when Cornelius revealed his giant bat form, Bowser BIT THE BAT'S WING. Waluigi wants to emphasize: he BIT a giant undead bat. This requires a level of immune system confidence that Waluigi does not possess and does not WANT to possess.

When the Shadow Anchor was revealed inside a shattered statue, Bowser threw Cornelius INTO the statue, breaking it open. Without Bowser's raw physical force, the Anchor might never have been exposed for Green T to shoot.

## The Vivian Fight

Bowser's performance during the Vivian corridor ambush was peak Bowser in every way:

**He dragged unconscious Markop to safety.** Not gently—by the tail, across stone floors—but EFFECTIVELY. Markop was alive because Bowser prioritized getting him out over fighting elegantly.

**He held the door.** Bowser braced against the maintenance room door with his full weight while Vivian hacked through it with an axe. Bowser's claws gouged the frame as he fought to keep it shut. The door eventually failed, but Bowser bought time that Markop needed to regain consciousness.

**He hit Vivian in the head.** When the door breached, Bowser struck Vivian across the skull—a blow that staggered the Corvinarus heir. In a fight where the enemy has death magic and supernatural pain tolerance, a solid punch to the head is still a solid punch to the head.

**He found the wand.** During the chaos, a necromancer's wand dropped from Vivian. Bowser picked it up, turned it over curiously, and said 'Ooooh. Is this a magic wand?'

Waluigi LOVES this detail. The party nearly died. Markop's armor was failing under a crimson death beam. Divine intervention was required for survival. And Bowser found a necromantic artifact and examined it like a toddler finding something interesting on the ground.

Bowser's complete inability to feel the appropriate level of dread in terrifying situations is either a character flaw or a SUPERPOWER. Waluigi has decided it's both.

## The Wand Question

Bowser asking 'Is this a magic wand?' while holding a necromancer's focus in a death dimension during an active combat situation is the most Bowser moment in the entire campaign.

Markop—still recovering from nearly being killed—managed 'I'm not sure.' Remi later confirmed it was indeed a necromancer's wand, cold to the touch and death-aspected.

Waluigi is genuinely uncertain whether Bowser's casual handling of the wand was DANGEROUS or PROTECTIVE. Necromantic artifacts typically corrupt or influence their wielders. But Bowser's magical sophistication is essentially ZERO. He doesn't understand what the wand does, doesn't respect its power, and doesn't fear its influence. Can you corrupt someone who doesn't understand they're supposed to be corrupted?

Waluigi suspects the wand is more confused by Bowser than Bowser is by the wand.

## Relationship with Disaster Inc.

Bowser's alliance with Disaster Inc. is one of the most unlikely partnerships in the campaign. Bowser is traditionally an ANTAGONIST—kidnapping princesses, conquering kingdoms, generally being the obstacle that heroes overcome.

But the Planar Fracture threw normal alignments into chaos. Bowser ended up on the same side as the party because the SITUATION demanded it. Vampires don't care about Mushroom Kingdom politics. The Shadowfell doesn't distinguish between heroes and villains. When everyone is trapped in a death dimension together, old rivalries become irrelevant and shared survival becomes paramount.

Bowser has adapted to this alliance with surprising grace. He follows Markop's tactical suggestions—not because he recognizes Markop's authority, but because Markop's suggestions are usually GOOD and Bowser respects competence even if he'd never admit it.

Waluigi finds this unexpectedly endearing. Bowser, the great villain, taking direction from a lizardfolk tactician because the alternative is dying in a vampire's hallway. Circumstances make strange allies.

## Assessment

Bowser is not the most skilled fighter in Disaster Inc. He's not the most magical or the most tactical or the most politically savvy.

Bowser is the most INDESTRUCTIBLE.

He takes hits that would kill anyone else and keeps fighting. He faces threats that would terrify anyone else and keeps punching. He finds necromantic artifacts in death dimensions and asks if they're magic wands with the curiosity of someone browsing a gift shop.

Waluigi has arm-wrestled Bowser. Waluigi LOST, which Waluigi attributes to the table being at the wrong height and NOT to any deficiency in Waluigi's arm strength, which is CONSIDERABLE.

But Waluigi respects Bowser. In a crisis, Waluigi wants Bowser nearby. Not for subtlety—Bowser doesn't DO subtlety. For SURVIVAL. Because when everything goes wrong and the death beams are flying, Bowser will hold the door, drag you to safety, hit the attacker in the head, and then find something interesting on the floor.

That's not elegance. That's RELIABILITY. And in the Shadow Estate right now, reliability might be worth more than anything.

WAH.

name: Valorian Stormweave
title: The Dead Man Who Took His Secrets With Him
status: Deceased — killed by Archie Miser in a public market, 1040 BF. Ruled 'justifiable magical defense' by Onyx Hand tribunal.
summary: Valorian Stormweave was a Senior Enforcer of the Mages' Guild who—according to Lady Bloomia's testimony—was present at the Royal Vault on the morning of Princess Peach's assassination in 955 BF. He allegedly delayed the Solstice Crown delivery, knew Bloomia's name without introduction, smiled 'like a predator who has confirmed the location of its prey,' and was part of the Guild's involvement in 'the arrangement.' He lived for eighty-five years after allegedly helping murder a princess. Then Archie Miser killed him in a public market during an altercation that an Onyx Hand tribunal ruled justifiable. The only person who could have testified about Guild complicity in the assassination is now ash. Whether this is cosmic justice, cosmic irony, or cosmic convenience depends entirely on who you ask—and EVERYONE has an opinion. Waluigi has spent considerable time examining this death because it sits at the intersection of two stories that should have nothing to do with each other: Archie's chaotic journey and the eighty-five-year-old assassination conspiracy. The intersection is either coincidence or something much worse. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Valorian Stormweave with the acknowledgment that most of what Waluigi knows about this man comes from two sources: Lady Bloomia's testimony (which may or may not be authentic) and the public record of his death at Archie Miser's hands (which is documented but contextually complicated). Between these two data points lies eighty-five years of a life Waluigi knows almost nothing about—a career in the Mages' Guild, a rise to Senior Enforcer, and whatever private knowledge he carried about one particular morning in 955 BF.

## The Morning of Highsun 1, 955 BF — Bloomia's Account

If Lady Bloomia's testimony is authentic—and Waluigi must emphasize the IF, because the Regency disputes Bloomia's entire existence—then Valorian Stormweave was present at the Royal Vault on the morning Princess Peach was assassinated.

Bloomia describes encountering two figures in dark robes embroidered with silver staves—Mages' Guild identification—arguing with the vault master Cornelius about 'unauthorized magical access' to the Solstice Crown's seals.

The taller mage was silver-haired, pale-eyed, with 'the particular condescension that the Guild cultivates like a hothouse flower.' He was DELAYING the crown delivery. The vault master insisted the seals were intact. The mage insisted Guild instruments detected irregularities. The crown could not be released until their 'investigation' was complete.

Then Bloomia arrived. The Princess had sent her to retrieve the crown personally.

The tall mage turned. He looked through Bloomia 'the way mages look through anyone who cannot cast.' Then he said her name.

'The handmaiden. Bloomia, yes?'

He KNEW her name. Without introduction. Without being told. A Senior Guild Enforcer knew the name of a seventeen-year-old handmaiden he had supposedly never met.

He then asked questions that demonstrated knowledge of what was happening in the Princess's chambers: 'Have you noticed anything unusual? Visitors at odd hours? Passages that seem to lead nowhere? Smells that don't belong?'

He was describing EXACTLY what Bloomia had observed that morning—the earth-and-pine smell of Thornpaw's visits, the shifted cushions, the passages Peach kept sending Bloomia away from. He KNEW about the secret visitor. He knew about the hatch.

Bloomia lied. 'No. Nothing unusual.'

He smiled. The smile of a predator who has confirmed the location of its prey.

'Of course not. Well, take the crown. We were just leaving.'

They stepped aside. Bloomia took the crown and ran.

As she ran, the tall mage called after her: 'Be careful, Bloomia. The wards have been behaving strangely today. Fluctuations in the protective enchantments.'

He was WARNING her. Not out of kindness—out of cruelty. He wanted her to know that something was happening and that she could not stop it. The wards were 'fluctuating' because the Guild was DISABLING them. The protective enchantments around the Princess's chambers were being deliberately weakened.

The tall mage was Valorian Stormweave.

## The Encoded Field Note — Guild Awareness

Bloomia later found a notation scratched into the vault's visitor log in a Guild field cipher—a number-substitution code that translates to:

'SUBJECT IS AWARE. THE HATCH IS OPEN. PROCEED AS PLANNED.'

This note—if authentic—confirms that the Guild knew about the secret hatch, knew the assassination was proceeding, and was coordinating their actions around the timeline. 'Subject is aware' likely refers to Peach herself, who had told Bloomia she knew something was coming.

Stormweave's presence at the vault was not coincidence. He was there to DELAY the crown delivery—keeping Bloomia away from the Royal Suite during the killing window. He was there to CONFIRM that the operation was on schedule. He was there to ensure that the Guild's piece of 'the arrangement' was executed with bureaucratic precision.

## The Eighty-Five Years — What Did Stormweave Know?

Valor Stormweave lived for eighty-five years after the assassination.

EIGHTY-FIVE YEARS.

He rose to the rank of Senior Enforcer within the Mages' Guild—a position of significant authority and institutional trust. He operated within the Guild's power structure for decades, presumably continuing to serve the organization that Bloomia accuses of facilitating the Princess's murder.

What did he know during those eighty-five years?

Did he know the identity of the assassin? He was in the vault that morning. He knew about the hatch. He knew the operation was 'proceeding as planned.' The Guild 'provided the method,' according to Toadsworth Sr.'s journals. Stormweave may have known WHO held the blade as well as who opened the door.

Did he know where the evidence went? The Guild took control of all 'magical evidence' after the assassination. What they collected, what they destroyed, what they concealed—Stormweave, as a Senior Enforcer, would have had access to classified operational records.

Did he know about Lady Bloomia? Guild operatives hunted Bloomia through the servant passages within hours of the assassination. One of them died when the Silent One intervened. Stormweave may have been involved in ordering that pursuit—or at least aware of it.

Did he know about Mario's 'reallocation'? If the Guild cooperated with the Regency to remove Mario before the assassination and to suppress his investigation afterward, Stormweave may have known the details—where Mario was sent, what happened to him, why he disappeared.

Every secret of the assassination conspiracy—every name on Peach's list, every detail of the arrangement, every piece of suppressed evidence—was potentially accessible to Valorian Stormweave for eighty-five years.

And then Archie Miser killed him in a market.

## The Death — Archie's Market Fight

The circumstances of Stormweave's death in 1040 BF are documented in the Onyx Hand's tribunal records:

Archie Miser and Valorian Stormweave were involved in an altercation in a public market. The altercation escalated to magical violence. Archie killed Stormweave. The Onyx Hand tribunal that examined the case ruled it 'justifiable magical defense.'

The specifics of what triggered the altercation are not extensively documented in Waluigi's sources. Market confrontations between mages can escalate for any number of reasons—territorial disputes, personal grudges, accidental magical interference, or simply two volatile personalities occupying the same space.

What matters is not the cause but the CONSEQUENCE: the one person who could have testified about Guild involvement in the assassination is dead.

## The Coincidence Problem — Was It Really Random?

Waluigi must address the uncomfortable question: was Stormweave's death actually a random market fight?

Arguments for coincidence:

**Archie didn't know.** There is no evidence that Archie knew who Stormweave was or what he had done eighty-five years ago. Archie was born long after the assassination. He had no connection to the conspiracy investigation. He had no reason to target Stormweave specifically.

**Market fights happen.** Mages argue. Arguments escalate. People die. This is not unusual in a kingdom that has been at war for eighty-five years.

**The tribunal ruled justifiable defense.** If Archie attacked Stormweave unprovoked, the tribunal would not have ruled in his favor. The ruling suggests Stormweave was the aggressor or at least equally responsible for the escalation.

Arguments against coincidence:

**The timing.** Stormweave survived eighty-five years. He was killed in 1040 BF—the same year that the assassination conspiracy began to unravel. Thornpaw was about to confirm the secret relationship at Fawful's gala. The Loyalists were closing in on the truth. Stormweave was becoming a liability.

**Who benefits?** The Guild benefits from Stormweave's death. The one person who could testify about their involvement is silenced permanently. No interrogation. No testimony. No accountability.

**Archie's entropy.** The Mages' Guild later described Archie's magic as 'bleeding entropy'—destabilizing reality around him. What if Archie was ATTRACTED to Stormweave—or Stormweave to Archie—through dimensional resonance? What if the market encounter was not random but INEVITABLE, caused by planar forces that brought entropy and conspiracy into collision?

**Guild manipulation.** The Guild subsequently employed Archie. They knew about his capabilities. They knew about his instability. What if the market encounter was ARRANGED—the Guild engineering a confrontation between their most dangerous secret-keeper and a volatile mage who would eliminate the problem without knowing he was doing the Guild's work?

Waluigi cannot determine whether the death was coincidence or conspiracy. Both explanations have problems. Neither is fully satisfying.

What Waluigi CAN say: the death is CONVENIENT. Convenient deaths should always be examined carefully. And the convenience benefits the Mages' Guild more than any other party.

## Bloomia's Response — A Debt Unknowingly Owed

Lady Bloomia—if she exists, if her testimony is authentic—added a note to her manuscript about Stormweave's death:

'Valorian Stormweave lived for eighty-five more years after helping murder my Princess. He was eventually killed by a mage named Archie Miser in a public market—"justifiable magical defense," the Onyx Hand ruled. I do not know Archie Miser. But I owe him a debt he will never know about.'

Then she added:

'The only man who could have testified about what the Guild knew that morning is now ash. Convenient. Very convenient.'

Bloomia sees the same pattern Waluigi sees. The witness is dead. The testimony is lost. The Guild's secrets died with the man who kept them.

Bloomia owes Archie a debt. Archie doesn't know the debt exists. He killed a man in a market fight and has no idea that the man he killed was the last living link to the assassination of Princess Peach.

The cosmic irony is STAGGERING. Archie—the walking disaster, the entropy-bleeder, the man who resolves everything with fireballs—accidentally destroyed the most important piece of evidence in an eighty-five-year-old murder investigation. Not through malice. Not through intention. Through the same chaotic violence that defines everything Archie touches.

Archie Miser: solving and destroying mysteries simultaneously, one fireball at a time.

## What Died With Stormweave — The Lost Testimony

The knowledge that Valorian Stormweave took to his grave:

**The Guild's exact role.** How many Guild operatives were involved? Who gave the orders? What specific actions did the Guild take—disabling wards, providing the assassination method, hunting Bloomia, suppressing evidence?

**The assassin's identity.** Stormweave was at the vault. He knew the hatch was open. He knew the operation was proceeding. He may have known who walked through that hatch with a blade.

**The evidence disposition.** The Guild took control of all magical evidence from the crime scene. What they found, what they kept, what they destroyed—Stormweave would have known.

**The ongoing cover-up.** Eighty-five years of institutional secrecy. Who participated? Who was compromised? What documents exist in sealed Guild archives that could expose the conspiracy?

**Mario's situation.** If the Guild was involved in Mario's 'reallocation' after his investigation threatened the cover-up, Stormweave may have known the details—where Mario was sent, who authorized it, what leverage was used.

All of this knowledge is gone. Destroyed in a market fight by a man who had no idea what he was destroying.

Unless Stormweave left records. Unless he wrote things down. Unless he told someone. Unless there are Guild archives somewhere that contain his personal files, his operational logs, his private notes.

The Mages' Guild does not discard records easily. They are BUREAUCRATS. They document everything. If Stormweave's knowledge exists in written form somewhere—in a sealed vault, in a classified archive, in the kind of institutional memory that organizations preserve against future need—then his death did not destroy the evidence. It merely made it harder to access.

Waluigi intends to pursue this line of investigation. The Guild keeps records. Records can be found. And somewhere in the Mages' Guild's archives, eighty-five years of Valorian Stormweave's career are documented in forms, reports, and classified files that may contain the truth about the morning Princess Peach was murdered.

Finding those records is now on Waluigi's list. Near the top.

Right after escaping the Feywild.

Right after the tennis match with Mario.

WAH.

name: Toad Lee
title: The Defenestrated Diplomat
status: Active — Exploring the Overgrown Manor
summary: Toad Lee continues to be the only reason Disaster Inc. hasn't been completely consumed by the Feywild. He reads the lore, manages the incredibly drunk Rakasha, and initiates combat when necessary. He recently survived being thrown out of a high-story window by a goblin guard, which Waluigi finds highly amusing but respects the commitment to the fight.
description:
Toad Lee is proving to be a surprisingly aggressive diplomat. While he initially served as the quiet, observant foil to Waluigi's loud magnificence, the Feywild is wearing on him.

**The Combat Pragmatist**
When Remi's mechanical dog was stolen by goblin servants looking for scrap metal, Toad Lee didn't bother with fey riddles. He barged into the servant's quarters (interrupting a goblin on the toilet) and demanded the dog back. In the ensuing sword fight, Toad Lee's shield was stolen by the guard Gregory. Toad Lee attempted a heroic acrobatic maneuver, failed spectacularly, and fell out the window. He was only saved because Azure manifested a spectral hand to catch him.

**The Lore Keeper**
While Hjumpik is busy throwing axes at bombs, Toad Lee is actually paying attention to the environment. He uncovered Lady Aurelian's diary, reading critical lore about 'The Grafting' and the arrival of the Iron Legion. Toad Lee is the brain of the Feywild operation, even if his acrobatic skills need serious work. Waluigi will offer him tennis lessons if they survive this.

name: Ryan
title: The Man Who Jumped
status: Active — location uncertain, last known contact with Rakasha spirit-walkers
summary: Ryan is the person who jumped off the Vigilance during the Iron Sky Breach rather than be captured by the Iron Legion. He jumped. Off an airship. In the sky. He survived—somehow—and was taken in by a Rakasha spirit-walker. Waluigi does not know Ryan's current status or location, but anyone who survives a jump like that has earned Waluigi's respect forever.
description:
Waluigi was not aboard the Vigilance when the Iron Legion boarded and captured it. He learned about Ryan's escape secondhand, and the account makes his stomach clench every time he thinks about it.

Ryan was cornered on the observation deck. Iron Legion troops closing from two directions. No exit except the door they were coming through and the railing behind him. Most people, in that situation, would surrender. Most people would calculate the odds—capture versus certain death—and choose capture.

Ryan jumped.

## The Jump

Waluigi needs to emphasize how INSANE this decision was. The Vigilance was flying. The drop to the ground was... Waluigi doesn't actually know how far, but it was FAR ENOUGH that surviving should have been impossible. Physics says you die. Biology says you die. Basic common sense says you die.

Ryan jumped anyway.

Something about the angle of descent, the air currents, hitting tree canopy in a way that distributed the impact across multiple surfaces—Ryan survived. Injured but alive. Waluigi does not fully understand the mechanics. Waluigi suspects Ryan doesn't either. What matters is that Ryan chose certain death over uncertain captivity and somehow found a third option that nobody knew existed.

Waluigi has been in desperate situations before. He has faced enemies, monsters, fairy courts, and mirror dimensions. He does not know if he would have the courage to jump off an airship with no guarantee of survival. He does not know if that's courage or desperation or something else entirely. What he knows is that Ryan did it, and Ryan lived, and that makes Ryan one of the bravest people Waluigi has ever encountered.

## The Rakasha Spirit-Walker

After the jump, Ryan was found by a Rakasha spirit-walker—a being associated with spiritual traditions and dimensional sensitivities that Waluigi does not have extensive knowledge of. The spirit-walker took Ryan in, treated his injuries, and... then what? Waluigi does not know. Ryan's thread diverged from the main narrative of the crisis at that point.

The Rakasha connection is intriguing. Spirit-walkers presumably have knowledge of dimensional boundaries, planar transitions, and the kind of metaphysical mechanics that might be relevant to repairing the Planar Fracture. Whether Ryan's encounter with the spirit-walker was coincidence or something more deliberate, Waluigi cannot say.

## Assessment

Ryan is out there somewhere. Separated from the rest of Disaster Inc., possibly learning things from Rakasha spirit-walkers, possibly preparing to rejoin the fight. Waluigi hopes he's healing. Waluigi hopes he's gathering strength. And Waluigi hopes that when the party reunites—and they WILL reunite, Waluigi refuses to accept otherwise—Ryan comes back with whatever wisdom or power the spirit-walkers have to offer.

Anyone who jumps off an airship and survives deserves to come back as something MORE than they were before. That's just narrative justice. WAH.

name: Bones
title: The Infiltrator Who Triggered the Massacre
race: Unknown (skilled at disguise, so identification is uncertain)
status: Injured — captured, stabbed by General Ironhand, fate uncertain
summary: Bones was one of the most capable operatives among the Liberated Toads—skilled in disguise, infiltration, and the kind of sustained deception that allowed him to pass as an Iron Legion soldier for days. His infiltration of Aegis Command was brilliant. His capture triggered Order 120. Bones carries the knowledge that his actions—however well-intentioned—led to the massacre of every Toad prisoner in Legion custody. Waluigi does not know how anyone carries that weight.
description:
Waluigi has to write about Bones carefully because the story of Bones is also the story of Order 120, and Waluigi has already written about Order 120 more than he wanted to.

Bones was skilled. REMARKABLY skilled. After the Vigilance fell to the Iron Legion, most people scattered or were captured. Bones grabbed equipment from a fallen Legionnaire, adopted their bearing, and BECAME a Legionnaire. He walked through checkpoints on forged credentials and sheer nerve. He attended briefings. He ate in Legion mess halls. He saluted officers who would have killed him if they knew who he was.

The Iron Legion's greatest weakness is its rigidity—it assumes that anyone following protocols belongs. Bones exploited this assumption with the precision of someone who understood exactly how to be invisible in plain sight. Waluigi could never do what Bones did; Waluigi is too DISTINCTIVE. But Waluigi can recognize skill, and Bones had skill in quantities that most infiltrators can only dream of.

## The Infiltration

Bones penetrated Aegis Command—the Iron Legion's primary fortress, their command center, their administrative heart. He passed through three security layers. He documented prisoner facilities. He witnessed the industrial efficiency with which the Legion processed captured Toads—case numbers, categorization, storage conditions that treated people as inventory.

The intelligence Bones gathered was valuable. It confirmed what many suspected: the Iron Legion was not just fighting a war; it was processing people through a system designed to strip away personhood and replace it with logistics. The lower levels of Aegis Command were organized for efficiency, and the efficiency was pointed at something horrible.

## The Capture

Bones was caught. Whether a biometric check flagged an inconsistency, or an informant sold him out, or simple bad luck intervened—the details are uncertain. What's certain is that his cover failed and he was detained.

General Ironhand handled the interrogation personally. Ironhand stabbed Bones during the questioning—not fatally, but precisely, making a professional point about consequences. The blade went where it would cause maximum pain without death, because Ironhand wanted Bones alive enough to understand exactly how badly he had failed.

The interrogation also revealed the Green Decoy—a duplicate posing as Speaker L. This discovery suggested that the intelligence war was deeper and messier than anyone had realized. Both sides had been deceiving each other at levels that neither fully understood.

## Order 120

General Ironhand's response to Bones' infiltration was Order 120: immediate execution of all Toad prisoners in Iron Legion custody.

Waluigi has written about this order extensively elsewhere. The summary: every prisoner, everywhere, killed because one infiltrator got caught. Administrative retaliation disguised as security response.

Bones was alive when the order was issued. Bones presumably heard the order, or heard about the order, or was told about the order as part of Ironhand's psychological pressure. Bones knows that his capture—however unavoidable it might have been—triggered the massacre.

Waluigi does not know how Bones carries this. The knowledge that your actions, even heroic actions, even necessary actions, led to the deaths of everyone you were trying to save... that is a weight that Waluigi cannot imagine bearing. Bones was doing the RIGHT thing. He was gathering intelligence that could have helped the Liberated Toads survive. He was taking impossible risks for his people. And the result was the worst outcome imaginable.

Waluigi hopes Bones survives whatever the Iron Legion does to him next. Waluigi hopes Bones eventually escapes. And Waluigi hopes that if Bones ever reads this, he understands that the fault lies with Ironhand, not with him. Ironhand CHOSE to issue Order 120. Ironhand could have chosen differently. The massacre was Ironhand's decision, not Bones'.

But Waluigi suspects Bones already knows this, and it doesn't help. Logic doesn't defeat guilt. Facts don't silence the voice that says 'if only I had done something different.' Bones will carry this forever, and all Waluigi can do is acknowledge that the burden is not his to carry alone.

WAH.

name: Earl Grey
title: The Man Who Exploded
status: Deceased — literally exploded during the Syndicate Showdown
summary: Earl Grey was the primary enforcer for the Tea Leaf Syndicate—a skilled fighter whose loyalty to Green T was matched only by his combat effectiveness. His death during the Syndicate Showdown was the single most dramatic exit Waluigi has ever witnessed: Roger's poisoned dagger interacted with something in Earl Grey's biology, and the man DETONATED. Waluigi's favorite hat was in the blast radius. Waluigi is still upset about the hat.
description:
Earl Grey was the Tea Leaf Syndicate's muscle—the person who handled problems that couldn't be solved with tea and conversation. While Green T maintained the Syndicate's refined image, Earl Grey enforced its will with the kind of physical capability that made people reconsider disagreeing with the organization.

Waluigi did not know Earl Grey well. Their interactions were limited to the tense period between the Tea Party Incident and the Syndicate Showdown, when the Syndicate was hemorrhaging power and Earl Grey was fighting desperately to preserve what remained. Waluigi respected his determination even while recognizing that the Syndicate was already doomed.

## Combat Capabilities

Earl Grey was, by all accounts, one of the best pure fighters aboard the Vigilance. He moved with efficiency that suggested extensive training, engaged multiple opponents simultaneously without apparent strain, and possessed physical capabilities that exceeded what his frame would suggest. During the Syndicate Showdown, he held his own against several attackers at once, buying time for Green T to do... whatever Green T was planning.

The fight might have gone differently if the poison hadn't intervened.

## The Explosion

Roger's poisoned dagger struck Earl Grey during the melee. Under normal circumstances, the poison would have caused paralysis, unconsciousness, or death through conventional means. Earl Grey's physiology was not conventional.

The poison interacted with SOMETHING in Earl Grey's body chemistry. An alchemical compound in his blood? A latent magical instability? A mutation from years of sampling the Syndicate's more experimental tea blends? Nobody has ever adequately explained what happened or why. What Waluigi knows is the RESULT.

Earl Grey exploded.

Not figuratively. Not 'he was hit so hard he flew apart.' His body DETONATED. Outward. In all directions. The sound was somewhere between a thunderclap and a wet pop—a sound that Waluigi heard clearly and wishes he hadn't. People ten feet away were knocked off their feet. Items scattered across the marketplace. Biological matter went everywhere.

Waluigi's favorite hat was in the blast radius. The hat—custom made, carefully maintained, one of Waluigi's most treasured possessions—was SPLATTERED. By EARL GREY. Waluigi knows this is a petty concern compared to the death of a person, but the hat was IMPORTANT to Waluigi and he's allowed to grieve.

## Legacy

Earl Grey's death ended the Syndicate Showdown effectively. The remaining Syndicate members—those few who hadn't been killed by Archie's fireball days earlier—either surrendered or fled. Green T survived, but his organization died with Earl Grey's detonation.

The marketplace where Earl Grey exploded reportedly smelled strange for days afterward. Nobody could agree on what exactly the smell was—ozone, chemicals, something organic, something else. The uncertainty made it worse. Waluigi avoided that part of the Vigilance until the smell faded, and even then, he found himself checking the floor for... residue.

Waluigi does not know what to say about Earl Grey as a person. He was loyal to his organization, fought hard for it, and died in a way that nobody expected. His death was the exclamation point on the Tea Leaf Syndicate's collapse—a dramatic, horrible, unexplainable end that matched the dramatic, horrible, unexplainable events of the entire campaign.

Rest in pieces, Earl Grey. Waluigi means that LITERALLY. WAH.

name: Dan (The Parallel Paradox)
title: The Multi-Dimensional Headache
status: Active — Split between 'Original', 'Parallel', and 'Purple T'
summary: There are too many Dans. The cautious survivor Waluigi knew has been replaced by a dimensional duplicate. The 'Parallel Dan' traveling with Markop admitted he shoved the original Dan into a Mages' Guild null cage to silence him. Meanwhile, another Toad operative ('Purple T') is hunting Archie. Waluigi is deeply frustrated by this. One bureaucrat is annoying; a multiverse of bureaucrats is a nightmare.
description:
Waluigi must attempt to explain a situation that gives him a migraine. 

During a rest in the Shadowfell forest, Markop cast a Zone of Truth and confronted Dan. Dan confessed that he was NOT the original Dan. He is a 'Parallel Dan' from the mirror dimension. He swapped places with the original Dan during a restaurant raid weeks ago.

**The Fate of the Original**
Parallel Dan admitted he didn't kill the original Dan. Instead, he handed the original over to the Mages' Guild, who locked him in a 'null cage'—a magical containment unit that nullifies all arcane abilities. The original Dan is currently trapped in a Mages' Guild barrack, wearing an associate badge (Number 447) that tracks his movements and burns him if he tries to remove it. He is a prisoner disguised as an initiate, hiding coded notes in his mattress.

**The Motive**
Parallel Dan claims he disrupted the Oracle's ritual because if the ritual had succeeded, the parallel reality would have collapsed, killing him. He replaced the original to ensure his own survival. It is a selfish, cowardly act that perfectly aligns with Dan's core philosophy of survival at any cost. Even across dimensions, Dan is consistent.

**Purple T and the Rogue Mages**
To make matters infinitely worse, another operative known as 'Purple T' (who may or may not be another variant of Dan, or just a very sneaky Toad) has gone rogue. Purple T, along with a zealot named Bryan (servant of the 'Toad God'), ripped off their Mages' Guild tracking badges. They are currently hunting Archie Miser, using Archie's 'Wahbook' tablet posts to track his location across dimensions. 

Waluigi's assessment is simple: Trust no Toad named Dan. If you see a Dan, assume he is a spy, a clone, or about to lock you in a cage. WAH.

name: Eager
title: The Magnet for Catastrophe
status: Active — recovered from spider grove capture
summary: Eager is the person whose rescue from the spider grove triggered the Battle of the Spider Grove. He has a supernatural gift for finding the worst possible place to be and BEING there. If there's a giant spider nest within ten miles, Eager will be inside it. If there's a bottomless pit, Eager will be sitting on its edge. Waluigi has mixed feelings about Eager—gratitude that rescuing him led to an excellent battle, frustration that the rescue was necessary in the first place.
description:
Waluigi does not know how Eager ended up cocooned in the Silent Grove. Waluigi suspects even EAGER doesn't fully know how Eager ended up cocooned in the Silent Grove. What Waluigi knows is that when the party needed to mount a rescue operation, Eager was suspended fifteen feet off the ground between two dead oaks, wrapped in spider silk like the world's worst piñata.

This is TYPICAL for Eager.

## The Catastrophe Magnet Effect

Eager seems to attract dangerous situations the way Wario attracts coins. It's not that Eager SEEKS danger—he doesn't seem to have a death wish or a thrill-seeking personality. Danger just FINDS him. He walks into rooms and discovers they're on fire. He takes shortcuts that lead through forbidden territories. He sits down to rest and ends up in a spider queen's web.

Waluigi has met unlucky people before. Waluigi considers himself somewhat unlucky (though Waluigi believes his 'bad luck' is actually SYSTEMATIC UNFAIRNESS). But Eager's relationship with catastrophe exceeds normal unluckiness. It's almost supernatural. If Eager ever figures out how to CONTROL this effect—direct it at enemies instead of himself—he'd be one of the most dangerous people in the setting.

## The Rescue and After

The party rescued Eager from the spider grove through a multi-phase battle that included titan wrestling, arcane rays, exploding spiders, and a banishment circle. Eager, for his part, contributed by deploying pepper spray against clusters of smaller arachnids while stuck in an enlarged form.

Pepper spray. Against spiders. And it WORKED.

Waluigi has to give Eager credit for creative thinking. Most people, stuck in a giant form in the middle of a spider battle, would not think to use pepper spray. Eager apparently carries pepper spray into situations where pepper spray should be useless, and then finds situations where it becomes useful. This is either preparation or luck, and Waluigi cannot tell which.

## Assessment

Eager is an asset and a liability in equal measure. His tendency to end up in dangerous situations creates opportunities for dramatic battles and valuable loot (the Spider Grove yielded excellent items). It also creates rescue obligations that drain resources and attention.

Waluigi has decided to view Eager as a quest generator. Wherever Eager is, there's probably a problem. That problem probably has treasure attached. So following Eager is, in a weird way, a viable strategy for acquiring wealth and experience, as long as you're prepared to fight whatever horrible thing has captured Eager THIS time.

WAH.

name: Smoking J
title: The Venomous Casualty
status: Active — recovering from spider venom
summary: Smoking J was bitten during the Battle of the Spider Grove and suffered a severe venomous reaction that forced his withdrawal from the front line. His incapacitation at a critical moment reduced the party's fighting strength during the most dangerous phase of the battle. Waluigi hopes Smoking J has fully recovered, though the long-term effects of arachnid venom are unpredictable.
description:
Smoking J was an active combatant during Phase 2 of the Spider Grove battle—the period when the grove's defenses were fracturing and smaller arachnids were converging from all directions. He was fighting alongside the main group when one of the dog-sized spiders landed a bite.

The venom hit FAST. Swelling. Disorientation. The kind of systemic reaction that says 'this biological agent does not belong in your body and your body knows it.' Smoking J had to be pulled back from the front line, reducing the party's combat strength at exactly the wrong moment.

## Impact on the Battle

Smoking J's incapacitation was one of several factors that made the Spider Grove battle so desperate. With Smoking J down, the remaining fighters had to cover more ground with fewer people. The toad squad got cut off partly because there weren't enough fighters to maintain a continuous line. Remi had to hold her position with only her mechanical dog as backup.

Waluigi is not assigning blame—Smoking J didn't CHOOSE to be bitten, and arachnid venom is not something you can shrug off through determination. But the tactical consequences of his withdrawal rippled through the rest of the engagement.

## Recovery

Waluigi does not know Smoking J's current status. The Planar Fracture scattered the party before Waluigi could confirm whether the venom's effects had fully resolved. Arachnid venoms are unpredictable—some cause immediate effects that fade quickly, others linger in the system for days or weeks, and some leave permanent damage.

Waluigi hopes Smoking J is fully recovered. Waluigi also hopes that if there ARE lingering effects, Smoking J has access to proper medical attention, though 'proper medical attention' is hard to find when reality has shattered into three pieces and everyone is trapped in hostile dimensions.

WAH.

name: Captain Syrup
title: The Pirate Queen of Rogueport
status: Active — Shelling everything in sight at Rogueport Bay
summary: Captain Syrup is the undisputed Pirate Queen of the seas, leader of the Black Sugar Pirates, and one of the few people whose greed might actually rival Wario's. She is currently engaged in a massive naval war in Rogueport Bay against the Iron Legion and the Mushroom Regency. Waluigi has a professional rivalry with Syrup. She thinks she's the best thief in the world. Waluigi *knows* he is.
description:
Waluigi respects Captain Syrup, though he would never admit it to her face. She runs a pirate empire with the kind of ruthless efficiency that Wario wishes he had. She doesn't bother with political ideologies or dimensional fractures. She sees a ship full of gold, she shoots cannons at it, she takes the gold. It is a wonderfully simple business model.

**The Battle of Rogueport**
Syrup and her fleet are currently the wildcard in the Coastal Provinces. The Iron Legion wants to blockade and tax the oceans. The Mushroom Regency wants to maintain order. Syrup just wants to sink both of them and loot the wreckage. 

When the Rakasha priest accidentally teleported the Toad scouts (Mystivl and Big R) directly onto a ship in Rogueport Bay, they arrived exactly as Captain Syrup yelled, 'Fire the cannons!' This is the quintessential Captain Syrup experience: arriving anywhere near her usually means you are about to explode.

**Assessment**
If the civil war continues to escalate, Syrup's naval superiority will become a massive factor. Whoever controls the sea controls the trade routes, and right now, Syrup is making sure nobody controls anything without paying her a toll in blood and cannonballs. Waluigi hopes to avoid Rogueport Bay until the smoke clears, but he fully intends to steal her ship someday just to see the look on her face. WAH.

name: Orvinder Danos
title: The Barrister of Truth
status: Active — In the Shadowfell, tracking planar anomalies
summary: Orvinder Danos is a lawyer in the Shadowfell. Yes, really. He is a barrister who values truth, justice, and the law, which makes him the single most out-of-place entity in a dimension ruled by manipulative, blood-sucking vampires. He assisted Archie in finding a dimensional portal. Waluigi profoundly distrusts lawyers, especially ones who claim to be honest and don't charge exorbitant fees.
description:
Orvinder Danos looks exactly like a well-to-do merchant or noble: neat dark hair, a mustache, keen eyes, and well-tailored clothing that lacks flashy ornamentation. He walks with a cane he does not actually need, which Waluigi recognizes as a classic theatrical prop to make opponents underestimate you.

**The Honest Lawyer**
Orvinder's defining trait is that he does not lie. Ever. He believes that laws must be upheld universally and unjust laws must be changed. He defends common folk against nobles. In the Shadowfell, where deceit is the primary currency, a man who strictly tells the truth is either completely insane or so powerful that he doesn't need to lie. Waluigi leans toward the latter.

**Planar Capabilities**
Orvinder encountered Archie while Archie was disguised as a guard. Orvinder saw right through it. More importantly, Orvinder demonstrated a staggering magical capability: he can open planar portals at certain 'reflection points.' He opened a portal to the ruined physical manor for Archie, explaining that it takes immense concentration but allows transit across the boundaries the Oracle broke.

Orvinder also seems to be acting as a guide or protector for Usk, attempting to reunite Usk's fragmented essence across the three manors. Why a barrister is involving himself in dimensional rescue operations is unclear. Perhaps he considers the Planar Fracture a violation of cosmic law. 

Waluigi would rather fight three dragons than be cross-examined by Orvinder Danos in a courtroom. WAH.

name: Vivian Corvinarus
title: The Impostor Heir
